question.message: The project is empty — no case, no demand file, no site data — so I need three things from you before the team can design anything: (1) where the site is (a place name or coordinates), (2) the demand (a file to upload with the heating/cooling load, or the services with their power), and (3) which services the plant must supply (heating, cooling, or both). If you would rather not gather that now, I can build the plant on the GEMINI hackathon example case instead.

answer.text: Use the GEMINI hackathon example case (hackathon-2026-*)

question.message: The GEMINI hackathon case's demand is two daily series files — `GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (column `heating_demand_MWth`) and `GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv` (column `cooling_demand_MWcool`), 365 daily values for 2027. Neither is in this project (it is empty) and neither is in the Knowledge base, so the case's two required demand series cannot be set from what I have. Please upload the two competition CSV files to the project. If you cannot, tell me and I will record the demand as open (the case cannot be completed without it).

answer.text: I do not know the details. Use your own reasonable assumptions for anything you need.

question.message:
Approve the case values for the GEMINI hackathon 2026 example case. All come from `knowledge/hackathon-2026-assumptions.md` (which restates the competition PDF p. 2 and the organisers' answers) unless marked otherwise.

TIME
- time_zone = UTC | agent assumption | the competition CSVs' `date` column has no offset and no file or user states the site's location; gemini's sample case uses UTC timestamps
- time.start 2027-01-01, time.end 2028-01-01 (excluded), time.step 1 d | doc, "Competition: Values from the files" (the CSVs' span)

DEMAND
- demand.heating.supply_temperature = 100 degC | doc (PDF p. 2, fixed)
- demand.heating.return_temperature = 60 degC | doc (team design choice)
- demand.heating.return_pressure = 6 bar | doc
- demand.cooling.supply_temperature = 20 degC | doc (PDF p. 2, fixed)
- demand.cooling.return_temperature = 25 degC | doc (team design choice)
- demand.cooling.return_pressure = 4 bar | doc
- demand.cooling.dew_point_margin = 1 K | doc
- demand.cooling.indoor_temperature = 26 degC | doc
- demand.cooling.indoor_relative_humidity = 50 % | doc

SITE
- site.ground.surface_temperature = 12 degC | doc (PDF p. 2)
- site.ground.gradient = 30 degC/km, uncertainty normal std 2 K/km, 25 to 35 K/km | doc
- site.reservoir.reference_depth = 2500 m | doc (PDF p. 2, midpoint TVD)
- site.reservoir.thickness = 100 m | doc (PDF p. 2, gross)
- site.reservoir.permeability = 200 mD, uncertainty triangular 100 to 400 mD | doc
- site.reservoir.pressure = 250 barg | doc (PDF p. 2)
- site.fluid.density = 1030 kg/m3 | doc (PDF p. 2)
- site.fluid.viscosity = 0.4 mPa.s | doc (PDF p. 2)
- site.fluid.gas_liquid_ratio = 0.8 Nm3/m3 | doc (PDF p. 2)
- site.fluid.dissolved_gas.CH4 = 0.8, .CO2 = 0.2 | doc (PDF p. 2, produced gas)
- site.fluid.sand_concentration = 20 mg/l | doc
- site.air.temperature = 10 degC (constant) | doc
- site.air.pressure = 101325 Pa (constant) | doc

UTILITIES
- utilities.electricity.co2_intensity = 300 g/kWh | doc (organisers)
- utilities.gas.composition: CH4 0.8249507401227822, C2H6 0.039549858193534584, C3H8 0.012748086337494389, CO2 0.011912342910726407, N2 0.11083897243546233 | doc (bought gas, digits as printed)

REQUIREMENTS (8, from the doc's "Competition: Requirements (8)")
- production_flow_range: doublet, production_flow, each, running, 50 to 300 m3/h
- brine_cooling_limit: doublet, brine_cooling, each, running, max 40 K
- running_time_limit: doublet, production_flow, duration, running, max 330 d
- pump_efficiency: doublet, pump_efficiency, 0.7 to 0.7 (no unit)
- full_reinjection: doublet, reinjection_ratio, each, running, 0.99999 to 1.00001
- doublet_count: doublet, count, 1 to 3
- heat_delivered: heating_supply, unmet_share, max 0.01
- cold_delivered: cooling_supply, unmet_share, max 0.01

Note: the two demand series (`GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv`, `GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv`) are still missing — they are not in the project, not in Knowledge and not on the web, and a series is never built from a peak and an annual energy. The case's two required demand powers therefore stay open.

The case is refused for one reason only: `demand.heating.power` and `demand.cooling.power` are required and the two competition demand files (GEMINI_Heating_Demand_Daily_2027.csv, GEMINI_Cooling_Demand_Daily_2027.csv) are not in the project, not in the Knowledge base and not on the web. A series is never built from a peak and an annual energy, so the only series-free form is a constant power. You said to use my own reasonable assumptions, so I propose, as engineering assumptions with no source:

- demand.heating.power = 30.0 MW constant | engineering assumption, no source | the brief's own heating peak (PDF p. 1, 30.0 MWth on 28 January); the demand file is unavailable, and a constant power at the stated peak is the only option that uses no number of mine. Consequence: the year's heat is far above the brief's 111.67 GWhth/year, so the plant will be oversized and the economics pessimistic.
- demand.cooling.power = 10.0 MW constant | engineering assumption, no source | the brief's own cooling peak (PDF p. 1, 10.0 MWcool on 19 July); same reason and same consequence against 23.74 GWhcool/year.

Uploading the two CSV files instead would give the real series and is much better. Approve all to set the case with these two constant powers, change some to give other values, or stop.
